body.translated_text: <s>Prajñāpāramitāpiṇḍārtha</s> (Summary of the Meaning of the Perfection of Wisdom)

children.translated_text: The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is non-dual knowledge (<s>advayajñāna</s>); that [non-dual knowledge] is the <s>Tathāgata</s>.
The goal [to be achieved], through fitness for that purpose, is expressed by that word [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] for both the text (<s>grantha</s>) and the path (<s>mārga</s>). // <s>Pppa</s> 1 //
The basis (<s>āśraya</s>), the subject matter (<s>adhikāra</s>), the action (<s>karma</s>), together with the practice (<s>bhāvanā</s>),
the divisions (<s>prabheda</s>), the characteristic mark (<s>liṅga</s>), and the culmination (<s>āpat</s>) — these are stated together with their benefits (<s>anuśaṃsa</s>). // <s>Pppa</s> 2 //
For those who have faith, the factors of engagement [are set forth]: the Teacher (<s>Śāstā</s>) and the assembly (<s>parṣat</s>) as witnesses,
and the place and time are indicated for establishing [the text's] own authority (<s>svaprāmāṇya</s>). // <s>Pppa</s> 3 //
For in the world, the compiler of the council (<s>saṅgītikartā</s>), when speaking of what is characterized by place and time,
with witnesses, the speaker attains authority (<s>prāmāṇya</s>). // <s>Pppa</s> 4 //
All this is the proclamation of hearing and the rest, which is of the nature of the <s>nidāna</s> (introduction);

children.text: prāsaṅgikaṃ tu evārthā mukhyā dvātriṃśadeva hi || 5 ||
children.translated_text: but the contextually relevant — the principal topics are exactly thirty-two. // <s>Pppa</s> 5 //
The division of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) in sixteen aspects, in due order,
is taught in the eight-thousand[-line version]; it should be understood through indirect designation (<s>anyāpadeśa</s>). // <s>Pppa</s> 6 //
Thus, the eight-thousand-[line text], with topics neither less [nor more] as stated,
is the desired abridgment of the text here; those very topics are as stated. // <s>Pppa</s> 7 //
'I do not see a <s>bodhisattva</s>' — thus the <s>Muni</s> (Sage) spoke in the ultimate sense;
thereby the emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) of the internal things (<s>ādhyātmikavastu</s>) — the enjoyer — is declared. // <s>Pppa</s> 8 //
'Form is empty of the intrinsic nature of form' — by this statement, again,
he negated the external sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) as objects of enjoyment (<s>bhojya</s>). // <s>Pppa</s> 9 //
In the absence of form and the rest, the characteristic of embodiment (<s>dehapratiṣṭhālakṣaṇa</s>) is destroyed;
by which that [internal] is seen as having served its purpose — thus the internal (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) is [also shown to be] non-existent. // <s>Pppa</s> 10 //
When the internal things are empty, there is also the emptiness of [their] nature (<s>prakṛti</s>);

for the spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>), which is of the nature of consciousness (<s>vijñānarūpa</s>), is understood to consist of compassion and wisdom (<s>kṛpāprajñātmaka</s>). // <s>Pppa</s> 11 //

children.text: notpanno na niruddho vā sattva ityādinā sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: 'A being is neither born nor ceased' — by such [statements], clearly,
the emptiness of both beings (<s>sattva</s>) and <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) is fully shown. // <s>Pppa</s> 12 //
'He does not see the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities (<s>buddhadharma</s>), nor the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s>' —
by such [statements], the [ten] powers (<s>daśabala</s>) and the rest are declared to be empty. // <s>Pppa</s> 13 //

children.text: prati prati yato dharmāḥ kalpitā iti kīrtitam /
children.translated_text: Since it is proclaimed that <s>dharmas</s> are fabricated (<s>kalpita</s>) in every respect,
therefore he also stated that there is no ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>) of <s>dharmas</s>. // <s>Pppa</s> 14 //
Because the great [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] eliminates the views of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) and the rest,
therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> proclaimed the selflessness of the person (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>) in every way. // <s>Pppa</s> 15 //
'All <s>dharmas</s> are unborn (<s>anutpanna</s>)' — by thus proclaiming,
the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>) was declared in every way by the knower of reality. // <s>Pppa</s> 16 //
Through the non-increase and non-decrease of blameworthy and blameless [<s>dharmas</s>],
the negation of wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>) [<s>dharmas</s>] — both conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) and unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). // <s>Pppa</s> 17 //

children.text: kuśalānāṃ ca śūnyatve tadgatā akṣatā tathā /
children.translated_text: When wholesome [<s>dharmas</s>] are empty, those pertaining to them are likewise unharmed;
it is merely fabricated (<s>kalpita</s>) — thus is the summary of the divisions of emptiness. // <s>Pppa</s> 18 //
Through ten distractions of the mind (<s>cittavikṣepa</s>), the mind is scattered elsewhere;
it becomes [only] fit for childish beings, not for the attainment of non-dual knowledge (<s>advayajñāna</s>). // <s>Pppa</s> 19 //
To remove those [distractions], mutually as opponents and counter-opponents (<s>vipakṣapratipakṣa</s>),
the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> text has shown them, and they are summarized [here]. // <s>Pppa</s> 20 //
When he says 'being a <s>bodhisattva</s>' — that is the fabrication of [inherent] existence (<s>abhāvaprakalpanā</s>);
the Teacher dispels [this] distraction through showing the conventional (<s>sāṃvṛta</s>) <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). // <s>Pppa</s> 21 //
By this, from the opening statement in the <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā</s> and other [texts],
up to the conclusion, the fabrication of non-existence (<s>abhāvakalpanā</s>) is to be negated by this method. // <s>Pppa</s> 22 //
These are not statements of reasons (<s>hetuvākya</s>); only the task [to be done] is indicated;
the reasonings are to be known everywhere from <s>sūtras</s> such as the <s>Brahmajāla</s> and others. // <s>Pppa</s> 23 //
'I do not see a <s>bodhisattva</s>, I' — by such elaborations,
the <s>Bhagavān</s> negates the delusion of conceptualizing [inherent] existence (<s>bhāvasaṅkalpa</s>). // <s>Pppa</s> 24 //

children.text: yanna paśyati nāmāpi gocaraṃ[na] kriyāṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: That he does not see even the name, nor the sphere [of activity], nor the action likewise,
nor the <s>skandhas</s> in any way — thereby he does not see a <s>bodhisattva</s>. // <s>Pppa</s> 25 //
This is the negation of the fabricated (<s>kalpita</s>) — such is the summary view;
every aspect that has risen to the status of being knowable (<s>jñeya</s>) is considered fabricated in cognition. // <s>Pppa</s> 26 //
For in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the teaching relies on three [natures]:
the fabricated (<s>kalpita</s>), the other-dependent (<s>paratantra</s>), and the fully perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>). // <s>Pppa</s> 27 //
By words such as 'does not exist' and the like, everything fabricated (<s>kalpita</s>) is negated;
through examples such as 'like an illusion' (<s>māyopama</s>) and the like, the other-dependent (<s>paratantra</s>) is taught. // <s>Pppa</s> 28 //
The teaching of the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> (perfected nature) through fourfold purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>);
for in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, there is no other teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>. (verse 29)
In the teaching-sequence that is the antidote to the ten conceptual projections (<s>saṅkalpavikṣepa</s>),
one should understand herein the collective and distributive declaration of the three [natures]. (verse 30)
As in the first statement, by the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> (perfected), <s>paratantra</s> (dependent), and <s>parikalpita</s> (imagined) [natures],
the removal of projection in the form of non-existence, conceptualization, and appearance [respectively]. (verse 31)

children.text: tena buddhaṃ tathā bodhiṃ na paśyāmīti vācakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, by expressions such as 'I do not see the <s>Buddha</s>' and 'nor do I see <s>bodhi</s> (awakening),'
the rejection of the imagined [nature] should be understood herein up to the conclusion [of the sūtra]. (verse 32)

children.text: śūnye rūpe svabhāvena samāropaḥ kva kena vā /
children.translated_text: When form is empty by its own nature, where and by whom is superimposition (<s>samāropa</s>) [possible]?
In other statements too, one should understand the removal of that [superimposition]. (verse 33)

children.text: na hi śūnyatayā śūnyamiti vākyaṃ vinirdiśan /
children.translated_text: The statement declaring 'the empty is not empty by emptiness'
has completely stated the removal of the conceptualizations of denial (<s>apavāda</s>). (verse 34)
'The <s>Buddha</s> is like a magical illusion (<s>māyopama</s>)' and also 'He is like a dream (<s>svapnopama</s>)' —
this same order should be known by the wise in other statements as well. (verse 35)
The <s>Jina</s> is said to be like a magical illusion through co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>);
and by words such as 'illusion-like,' the dependent nature (<s>paratantra</s>) is expressed. (verse 36)
The knowledge of ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) that naturally brings about purification —
that is designated by the word '<s>Buddha</s>,' just as a <s>Bodhisattva</s> [is called] a <s>Jina</s>. (verse 37)
Concealing its own true nature, controlled by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>),
it appears otherwise like a magical illusion, and relinquishes the fruit like a dream. (verse 38)
In the false declaration of the non-dual, or in [denying] the fruit of the deniers —
this is said to be the denial of the conceptualizations of denial (<s>apavāda</s>). (verse 39)
Form and emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) cannot be conjoined, due to their mutual contradiction;
emptiness is without form; name and form are connected with appearance (<s>ākāra</s>). (verse 40)
Thus, having refuted the conceptualization of oneness (<s>ekatva</s>), the conceptualization of difference (<s>nānātva</s>)
is also blocked — no other form of that exists in emptiness in any way. (verse 41)
Since the non-existent appears, that is constructed by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>);
by the very power to make the non-existent appear, it is called '<s>avidyā</s>' (ignorance). (verse 42)
This very thing is called 'form' (<s>rūpa</s>) and also '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>';
the non-dual (<s>advaya</s>) is this very duality — the refutation of both conceptualizations. (verse 43)
And he states the reasoning: by purity, and by non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>),
and by the contradiction of existence and non-existence — one also perceives diversity. (verse 44)
This form is mere name; in reality it is without own-nature (<s>asvabhāva</s>);
this excludes the scope of the conceptualizations of its own-nature. (verse 45)
'Form is empty by the nature of form' — what was first stated
is the prohibition of the conceptualization of superimposing that own-nature. (verse 46)

children.text: notpādaṃ na nirodhaṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ paśyatīti yat /
children.translated_text: 'He sees neither the arising nor the cessation of <s>dharmas</s>' — that which
the <s>Bhagavān</s> stated is the detailed conceptualization of the particular [aspects] of that. (verse 47)

children.text: kṛtrimaṃ nāma vācyāśca dharmāste kalpitā yataḥ /
children.translated_text: Names are artificial, and those <s>dharmas</s> that are objects of speech are imagined (<s>kalpita</s>);
there is no connection between word and meaning — hence it is held not to be inherent (<s>svābhāvika</s>). (verse 48)
The attachment to external objects arises through the confusion of the childish;
similarly this convention — but there is some meaning here. (verse 49)

children.text: atra tena yathā nāma kalpyate na tathāsti tat /
children.translated_text: Here, just as a name is imagined, the designated thing does not exist thus;
therefore the conclusion is: the conceptualization of meaning follows the name. (verse 50)
'<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,' '<s>Buddha</s>,' and '<s>Bodhisattva</s>' likewise —
he declared [these] to be mere names, dispelling the conceptualization of real meaning. (verse 51)
This is the denial of word and meaning; the entity (<s>vastu</s>) itself is not denied;
similarly in other statements too, the determination of meaning should be known. (verse 52)
The knower of reality does not perceive all names
as corresponding to reality; therefore this is not the denial of sound [itself]. (verse 53)

children.text: subhūtistu dvayaṃ vyasan śabdaṃ śabdārthameva ca /
children.translated_text: But <s>Subhūti</s>, dispelling both — sound and the meaning of sound —

children.text: bodhisattvasya no nāma paśyāmīti sa uktavān || 54 ||
children.translated_text: said: 'I do not see the name of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' (verse 54)
There is no statement of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> whose implied meaning (<s>neyatā</s>) has not been shown;
those meanings should merely be inferred with subtle intelligence. (verse 55)
The concealment of the stated meaning and the imagination of another meaning —
in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, that is called '<s>prativarṇikā</s>' (counter-annotation). (verse 56)
This is the brief summary of meaning based on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>;
that same meaning is repeated, based on further meanings. (verse 57)
Having correctly summarized the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) in Eight Thousand Lines,
by whatever merit has been obtained thereby, may people become perfected in <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom)! (verse 58)

body.translated_text: The Compendium of the Essential Meaning of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) is complete.
This is the work of the teacher <s>Dignāga</s>.
